title: Microsoft Teams: separate attendance and engagement report policy for Teams events
summary: The rollout window, report settings, licensing qualifications and controls table are supported. One actionable instruction needs correction: the Events policies landing page is not a documented route for checking each user's effective policy; keep the documented PowerShell alternative instead.

claims.claim: This roadmap item concerns Microsoft Teams.
claims.quote: "products": ["Microsoft Teams"]

claims.claim: Microsoft plans independent attendance and engagement report controls for events in CsTeamsEventsPolicy and meetings in CsTeamsMeetingPolicy.
claims.quote: administrators can independently manage organizer access to attendance and engagement reports for Teams Events through CsTeamsEventsPolicy, without affecting attendance and engagement report settings for Teams Meetings managed through CsTeamsMeetingPolicy.

claims.where: What's changing; Why it matters; controls[2].note; Governance controls
claims.claim: The current Learn attendance report article describes the meeting policy setting as applying to both meetings and events.
claims.quote: Organizers with this policy can view and download the attendance and engagement reports for all meetings and events they create.

claims.claim: The Set-CsTeamsEventsPolicy reference marks the events policy as still in preview.

claims.where: controls[0].scope; Risk assessment: Security & identity; Scope; Governance controls
claims.claim: The events setting is a user-level policy control for organisers' event reports.
claims.quote: User-level policy for tenant admin to configure options for customizing Teams events experiences. Use this cmdlet to update an existing policy.

claims.claim: Set-CsTeamsEventsPolicy -Identity <policy name> -AllowEngagementReport ForceDisabled blocks organisers from viewing or downloading event reports.
claims.quote:
Set-CsTeamsEventsPolicy -Identity Global -AllowWebinars Disabled
Controls whether attendance and engagement reports are allowed for events.
**ForceDisabled**: Off. Organizers cannot view or download attendance and engagement reports.

claims.claim: The events parameter value Enabled corresponds to On, organizers can turn it off.
claims.quote: **Enabled**: On, but organizers can turn it off.

claims.claim: The events parameter value Disabled corresponds to Off, organizers can turn it on.
claims.quote: **Disabled**: Off, but organizers can turn it on.

claims.claim: The events parameter value ForceEnabled turns reports on without an organiser override.
claims.quote: **ForceEnabled**: On. Organizers cannot turn off attendance and engagement reports.

claims.claim: The events parameter value ForceDisabled corresponds to Off with no organiser report access.
claims.quote: **ForceDisabled**: Off. Organizers cannot view or download attendance and engagement reports.

claims.where: controls[0].ui; Scope; Governance controls; Open questions
claims.claim: At the time of writing, Learn documents no Teams admin center path for the new events report setting.
claims.quote: Searched: Teams events policy AllowEngagementReport attendance engagement report Teams admin center Events policies setting. Opened meeting-attendance-report, meeting-policies-overview and Set-CsTeamsEventsPolicy; inspected settings-policies-reference search excerpts.

claims.claim: Teams admin center > Meetings > Events policies > policy > Edit is the documented route for editing an events policy.
claims.quote:
go to **Meetings** > **Meeting policies** or **Events policies**.
2. Choose the policy by clicking to the left of the policy name, and then select **Edit**.

claims.claim: Grant-CsTeamsEventsPolicy -Identity <user> -Policy <policy name> assigns an events policy to a user.
claims.quote:
Grant-CsTeamsEventsPolicy -Identity "user1@contoso.com" -Policy DisablePublicWebinars
The command shown in Example 1 assigns the per-user Teams Events policy, DisablePublicWebinars, to the user with the user principal name (UPN) "user1@contoso.com".

claims.claim: The Grant-CsTeamsEventsPolicy reference also marks the policy as preview.
claims.quote: Assigns Teams Events policy to a user, group of users, or the entire tenant. Note that this policy is currently still in preview.

claims.where: controls[1].note; Risk assessment: Security & identity; Governance guidance
claims.claim: A user can be assigned only one events policy at a time.
claims.quote: A user can be assigned only one meeting policy and one events policy at a time.

claims.claim: Assigning a custom events policy replaces the global events policy for that user.
claims.quote: Users get the global policy unless you create and assign a custom policy.

claims.claim: The meeting report control is at Teams admin center > Meetings > Meeting policies > policy > Meeting scheduling > Attendance and engagement report.
claims.quote:
go to **Meetings** > **Meeting policies**.
2. Select the policy you want to update or create a new policy.
3. Go to the **Meeting scheduling** section.
4. Choose one of the following options for **Attendance and engagement report**:

claims.claim: Set-CsTeamsMeetingPolicy -Identity <policy name> -AllowEngagementReport Disabled turns off meeting-policy attendance and engagement reports.
claims.quote:
To turn off attendance and engagement reports, use the following script:
Set-CsTeamsMeetingPolicy -Identity <policy name> -AllowEngagementReport Disabled

claims.where: Why it matters; Risk assessment: Data exposure
claims.claim: Attendance and engagement reports identify who attended a meeting or event.
claims.quote: The report shows who attended a meeting or event

claims.where: Why it matters; Risk assessment: Data exposure
claims.claim: The reports include attendee join and leave times.
claims.quote: along with the exact times each attendee joined and left, and other engagement metrics.

claims.where: Why it matters; Risk assessment: Data exposure
claims.claim: Engagement information counts attendees who unmuted.
claims.quote:
The engagement data shows the total count of attendees that performed the following actions:
- Unmuted during the meeting or event

claims.where: Why it matters; Risk assessment: Data exposure
claims.claim: Engagement information counts attendees who turned on cameras.
claims.quote:
The engagement data shows the total count of attendees that performed the following actions:
- Unmuted during the meeting or event
- Turned on their cameras

claims.where: Why it matters; Risk assessment: Data exposure
claims.claim: Engagement information counts attendees who raised hands.
claims.quote:
The engagement data shows the total count of attendees that performed the following actions:
- Unmuted during the meeting or event
- Turned on their cameras
- Raised their hands

claims.where: Why it matters; Risk assessment: Data exposure
claims.claim: Engagement information counts attendees using meeting reactions.
claims.quote:
The engagement data shows the total count of attendees that performed the following actions:
- Unmuted during the meeting or event
- Turned on their cameras
- Raised their hands
- Used each type of meeting reaction

claims.where: Why it matters; Risk assessment: Data exposure
claims.claim: Engagement information counts attendees interacting through Q&A.
claims.quote: Initiated questions, answers, and discussions through Q&A.

claims.claim: Administrators cannot view attendance and engagement reports for events they did not organise.
claims.quote: As an admin, you can’t view the attendance and engagement report for meetings and events that you didn't organize.

claims.claim: Administrators can view attendees' details for an event within 24 hours of it.
claims.quote: you can view attendees' details for a given meeting or event within 24 hours of that meeting or event.

claims.claim: Attendee details are under Users > Manage users > organizer > Meetings & calls > meeting or call ID > Participant details.
claims.quote: go to **Users** > **Manage users**. Choose the display name for the meeting organizer. Select the **Meetings & calls** tab, and then choose the appropriate meeting ID or call ID. Then, select **Participant details**.

claims.claim: The policy assignment overview linked from the meeting policies article documents other assignment methods.
claims.quote: Assign a policy directly to users, either individually or at scale through a batch assignment, or to a group that the users are members of.

claims.claim: Get-CsUserPolicyAssignment -Identity <user> can be used to check a user's effective policy assignments.
